findings_qualitative.value: IRAS 15398-3359 harbors a compact hot corino within the 50 au area around the protostar, making it a hybrid chemical source with warm carbon-chain chemistry on large scales (100-1000 au) and hot corino chemistry on small scales (~10 au).

evidence.quote: These results, in combination with previous reports, indicate that IRAS 15398$-$3359 is a source with hybrid properties showing both hot corino chemistry rich in complex organic molecules on small scales $\sim$10 au) and warm carbon-chain chemistry (WCCC) rich in carbon-chain species on large scales ($\sim$100-1000 au).

findings_qualitative.value: The high-excitation CH3OH emission is predominantly blueshifted and slightly extended toward the northwest along the disk midplane (P.A. 130 deg), which may trace a thin surface layer of the disk structure heated by accretion shocks and/or protostellar irradiation.

evidence.quote: The distribution of the blueshifted component is concentrated within the 50 au area around the continuum peak position, with a slight extension along the disk midplane (P.A 130$^\circ$) toward the northwest.

evidence.loc: Small Beam Filling Factor vs. Slight Extension toward the Northwest
evidence.quote: One possibility which we speculate is that the CH$_3$OH emission could arise from the thin surface layer of the disk structure, as indicated by the yellow part in the schematic illustration of Figure 1(d).

claims.hypothesis: The prototypical WCCC protostellar source IRAS 15398-3359 also harbors a compact hot corino in the immediate vicinity of the protostar, making it a hybrid chemical source.
claims.experiment: Observed IRAS 15398-3359 at 0.2''-0.3'' resolution in ALMA Band 6 as part of the FAUST Large Program, extracted spectra toward the continuum peak, identified CH3OH, CH2DOH, and CH3OCHO lines, and performed a non-linear least-squares LTE fit to 9 CH3OH lines.
claims.result: Detected 9 CH3OH lines with E_u up to 537 K (plus one CH2DOH line and two blended CH3OCHO features), deriving T_rot = 119 +20/-26 K, N(CH3OH) = 3.2 +2.5/-1.0 x 10^18 cm^-2, and a beam filling factor of 0.018 +0.005/-0.003 within a 50 au region.
claims.finding: IRAS 15398-3359 harbors a compact hot corino and is a hybrid source exhibiting both WCCC on 100-1000 au scales and hot corino chemistry on ~10 au scales.

evidence.quote: We detect nine CH$_3$OH lines including the high excitation lines with upper state energies up to 500 K. The CH$_3$OH rotational temperature and the column density are derived to be 119$^{+20}_{-26}$ K and 3.2$^{+2.5}_{-1.0}	imes$10$^{18}$ cm$^{-2}$, respectively.

These results, in combination with previous reports, indicate that IRAS 15398$-$3359 is a source with hybrid properties showing both hot corino chemistry rich in complex organic molecules on small scales $\sim$10 au) and warm carbon-chain chemistry (WCCC) rich in carbon-chain species on large scales ($\sim$100-1000 au).

claims.hypothesis: The abundance ratios of CH2DOH and CH3OCHO relative to CH3OH in the hot corino of IRAS 15398-3359 are comparable to those in other hot corino and hybrid protostellar sources.
claims.experiment: Measured integrated intensities of CH2DOH (234.471 GHz) and two blended CH3OCHO features (234.5 GHz and 247.1 GHz) and calculated column densities under LTE assuming the same T_rot and beam filling factor as CH3OH.
claims.finding: IRAS 15398-3359 shows moderate deuterium fractionation and substantial CH3OCHO abundance comparable to other low-mass protostars harboring a hot corino (such as CB68, L1551 IRS5, and IRAS 16293-2422B).

evidence.quote: 3. The CH$_2$DOH/CH$_3$OH and CH$_3$OCHO/CH$_3$OH ratios in IRAS 15398$-$3359 are derived to be 0.03-0.20 and 0.02-0.15, respectively.

The CH$_2$DOH/CH$_3$OH ratio in IRAS 15398$-$3359 indicates that the deuterium fractionation level is comparable to those in the other low-mass protostars harboring a hot corino except for B335. As well, the CH$_3$OCHO/CH$_3$OH ratio in IRAS 15398$-$3359 is found to be similar to those in the sources CB68 (cite: Imai et al.(2022)), L1551 IRS5 (cite: Bianchi et al.(2020)), and IRAS 16293-2422B (cite: Jorgensen et al.(2018)).

claims.hypothesis: The small CH3OH beam filling factor (0.018, corresponding to a 4 au round Gaussian) and the slight spatial extension toward the northwest (~20-30 au) can be reconciled if the CH3OH emission arises from a thin surface layer of the edge-on disk heated by accretion shocks and/or protostellar irradiation.
claims.experiment: Compared the stacked integrated-intensity map and velocity profiles of the three CH3OH lines with E_u > 400 K against the known SO Keplerian disk orientation and rotation direction, and evaluated free-fall accretion velocity at r = 2 au.
claims.result: Blueshifted CH3OH emission extends slightly toward the northwest along the disk midplane (P.A. 130 deg), matching the blueshifted side of the SO disk rotation, with a velocity shift of ~3 km s^-1 comparable to the free-fall velocity of 2.4 km s^-1 at r = 2 au, though redshifted emission is weak/absent.
claims.finding: The CH3OH emission plausibly arises from a thin surface layer of the disk structure, but the kinematics and vertical structure cannot be definitively established at the current angular resolution.

evidence.loc: Small Beam Filling Factor vs. Slight Extension toward the Northwest
evidence.quote: One possibility which we speculate is that the CH$_3$OH emission could arise from the thin surface layer of the disk structure, as indicated by the yellow part in the schematic illustration of Figure 1(d).

evidence.loc: Small Beam Filling Factor vs. Slight Extension toward the Northwest
evidence.quote: In any case, the present observation cannot allow us to discuss further detailed kinematics of the CH$_3$OH emitting region.

evidence.loc: Small Beam Filling Factor vs. Slight Extension toward the Northwest
evidence.quote: To examine this hypothesis, we need higher angular resolution observations to resolve the vertical structure of the disk.

why_this_data.value: High-resolution (0.2''-0.3'', ~30 au) and high-sensitivity ALMA Band 6 observations from the FAUST Large Program are needed to probe the ~10-50 au region around the protostar without contamination from the 100-1000 au scale outflow and envelope.

evidence.quote: Hot corinos have been identified even in some sources which were hitherto classified as a WCCC source abundant in carbon-chain molecules, owing to high-resolution and high-sensitivity observations.

Since their CH$_3$OH spectrum is averaged over the 2$''$ ($\sim$300 au) area around the continuum peak, it traces a larger structure on a few 100 au scale. Rather, part of the outflow feature is likely contaminating the emission.

why_this_method.value: Simultaneous non-linear least-squares LTE fitting of 9 CH3OH lines spanning E_u = 61-537 K allows separate determination of rotation temperature, column density, and beam filling factor because the lines have moderate optical depths (not optically thin) and high H2 density (>10^7-10^8 cm^-3) near the protostar justifies LTE.

evidence.quote: The LTE condition is generally justified near the protostar ($\sim$10 au scale) where the H$_2$ density is 10$^7-$10$^8$ cm$^{-3}$ or higher (cite: Jorgensen et al.(2013); Sakai et al.(2014a)).

Note that the column density and the beam filling factor can be determined separately because the lines are not optically thin (Table 2). Approximately, the relative strength of the lines provides a measure of the excitation temperature and the column density, while the actual intensities provide a measure of the beam filling factor.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Fitting only the 5 CH3OH lines with E_u < 350 K to avoid potential infrared pumping of the E_u > 400 K lines; yielded similar best-fit parameters (107 K, 2.4x10^18 cm^-2, f=0.021) but rejected due to heavy parameter degeneracy and poor constraints.

evidence.quote: To assess this possibility, we tried to conduct a similar analysis by using the 5 lines of $E_uk_{m B}^{-1}$ $<$ 350 K. The best fit values of the rotation temperature, the column density, and the beam filling factors obtained from the 5 lines are 107 K, 2.4$	imes$10$^{18}$ cm$^{-2}$, and 0.021, respectively, which are not very different from those derived from all the lines. However, the parameters are not well constrained due to heavy correlation among the parameters, according to the error estimation using the $\chi^2$ values.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Alternative explanations for the weak redshifted CH3OH emission: foreground gas absorption at systemic velocity, an inverse P-Cygni profile from infalling gas onto the disk, dust shielding of the redshifted outflow launching point by the disk midplane, or an asymmetric gas distribution.

evidence.loc: Small Beam Filling Factor vs. Slight Extension toward the Northwest
evidence.quote: The absorption at the systemic velocity (5.5 km s$^{-1}$) might be caused by the absorption due to the foreground gas, but an inverse P-cygni profile could more reasonably explain the asymmetric spectral profiles of CH$_3$OH lines (Figure 1(c)).

evidence.loc: Small Beam Filling Factor vs. Slight Extension toward the Northwest
evidence.quote: If the CH$_3$OH emission comes from the launching point of the primary outflow, its redshifted part could be shielded by dust of the disk midplane. It should also be noted that the weak redshifted emission could also originate from asymmetric distribution of the CH$_3$OH emitting gas.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Photodesorption of CH3OH on the disk surface: rejected in favor of thermal desorption / accretion shock heating because laboratory experiments show CH3OH photodesorption is inefficient.

evidence.loc: Small Beam Filling Factor vs. Slight Extension toward the Northwest
evidence.quote: Note that photodesorption of CH$_3$OH is inefficient, as shown by the laboratory experiments (cite: Bertin et al.(2016); Cruz-Diaz et al.(2016)). Thus, thermal desorption in the surface layer should be considered here.

limitations_admitted.value: The CH3OH emitting region is much smaller than the synthesized beam size and is spatially unresolved.

evidence.quote: The beam filling factor is derived to be 0.018$^{+0.005}_{-0.003}$, indicating that the emitting region of CH$_3$OH is much smaller than the synthesized beam size and is not resolved.

limitations_admitted.value: The redshifted component is not clearly detected in the CH3OH lines, preventing a detailed kinematic analysis or confirmation of the disk surface origin without higher angular resolution observations.

evidence.quote: Unfortunately, we do not see the redshifted component clearly in the CH$_3$OH lines to discuss the kinematics in detail.

evidence.loc: Small Beam Filling Factor vs. Slight Extension toward the Northwest
evidence.quote: In any case, the present observation cannot allow us to discuss further detailed kinematics of the CH$_3$OH emitting region.

limitations_admitted.value: The lower-excitation CH2DOH line at 247.6257463 GHz (E_u = 29 K) predicted by the LTE model is not detected at the 3 sigma level, possibly due to foreground absorption or proximity to the correlator band edge.

evidence.quote: However, it is not seen with the 3$\sigma$ confidence level in IRAS 15398$-$3359, although it is expected to be deteted in the calculation (Figure 2 (d)). We do not fully account for this non-detection, but here note two possibilities. Since this line is quite low-excitation, it would be seriously affected by the absorption due to the extended foreground gas. Alternatively, the line is very close to the band edge of the correlator, which would provide a less accurate calibration.

limitations_admitted.value: CH2DOH and CH3OCHO column densities rely on assuming the same rotation temperature and beam filling factor as CH3OH because only one line of CH2DOH and two blended features of CH3OCHO are detected.

evidence.quote: Since only one line is available for CH$_2$DOH, the rotation temperature and the beam filling factor are assumed to be the same as those determined for CH$_3$OH, and the line width is employed for the average value of the CH$_3$OH lines (3.4 km s$^{-1}$).

referee_caveats_inferred: Setup 1 and Setup 2 have different synthesized beam sizes (~0.34'' x 0.29'' vs ~0.20'' x 0.18'', differing by a factor of ~2.7 in beam area), yet a single beam filling factor (f = 0.018) appears to be fit simultaneously across all 9 lines from both setups without explicit mention of convolving the cubes to a common resolution.

Noticeable discrepancy in Section 2 text vs Table 1 regarding array configurations: the text says C43-5 and C43-2 were combined, whereas Table 1 lists C43-5 and C43-2 for Setup 1, and C43-4 and C43-1 for Setup 2.

Dust optical depth at 1.2 mm toward the continuum peak is not subtracted or accounted for in the radiative transfer equation (Equation 1 only uses B_nu(T_cmb) as the background), although continuum brightness temperature is ~4.39 K.
